page: Hetzner Cloud cx23 belongs to the Cost Optimized server family, operating as a virtualized instance on a QEMU hypervisor. The system provides 2 shared vCPUs running on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, backed by 16 MB of L3 cache and 4 MB of L2 cache. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of total system RAM, supplying approximately 1.95 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled as a 40 GB NVMe SSD. The server does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 networking.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the entry-level baseline of the shared-core hardware profile. Synthetic processing evaluations place the cx23 in the lower percentiles across general compute metrics, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 649.0 and a multi-core score of 1161.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 2097.92. Memory bandwidth reaches 20.56 GB/sec on uncached reads and 17.58 GB/sec on uncached writes. Under service-specific tests, the instance achieves 1.24 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and delivers 1.84 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Machine learning execution is limited to lightweight inference, generating 43.07 tokens per second on a small 135M model.

The primary tradeoff of the cx23 centers on shared CPU allocations and conservative clock rates, which restrict multi-threaded parallel throughput. However, the inclusion of local NVMe storage and basic vector instruction support, including AVX-512F and AES, provides solid baseline I/O and cryptographic efficiency for cost-sensitive operations. The server is practical for low-intensity applications such as staging environments, microservices, light reverse proxies, development sandboxes, and personal web utilities.
description: Hetzner Cloud cx23 is an entry-tier virtual instance in the Cost Optimized series, powered by 2 shared vCPUs on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4.0 GB of RAM, a 40 GB local NVMe SSD, and lacks discrete GPU hardware. Hardware capabilities support modern instruction sets including AVX-512F and AES, though overall computational throughput is constrained by its shared vCPU allocation. Benchmark results show modest compute capacity, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1161.0, PassMark CPU score of 2097.92, and Redis SET throughput of 1.24 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth registers 20.56 GB/sec on large-block uncached reads. Delivering resource economy over sustained compute power, the cx23 is primarily suited for lightweight utility workloads, low-traffic web serving, microservices, development environments, and small-scale automation tasks that do not demand dedicated CPU cycles.
